item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.description: A Re-Examination of the Bridge to Nowhere Every few years, a trial is published comparing “better” CPR to standard CPR. More time on the chest. Greater depth. What are generally considered higher quality compressions. CPR that, in theory, should improve coronary perfusion pressure, increase the likelihood of ROSC, and ultimately improve patient outcomes. item.title: Efficacy and Safety of Tozorakimab in Patients Hospitalised for Viral Lung Infection Requiring Supplemental Oxygen
item.description: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effect of tozorakimab, as an add-on to SoC in patients with viral lung infection requiring supplemental oxygen, on the prevention of death or progression to IMV/ECMO.

item.title: A Trial of Adjunctive Fludrocortisone (50mcg, 100mcg or Placebo) in Critically Ill Patients With Septic Shock Receiving Hydrocortisone, Evaluating Survival and Functional Recovery and the Influence of Transcriptomic Response
item.description: The FLUDRO-SHOCK trial is a large international randomised controlled double-blinded study aiming to improve treatment for people with septic shock, a life-threatening condition caused by severe infection. Patients with septic shock receive a steroid called hydrocortisone, but it is unclear whether adding another steroid, fludrocortisone, improves their chances of recovery and survival. item.description: Currently, continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) is the main modality for renal support in critically ill patients with hemodynamic instability. Most studies have investigated the timing of RRT initiation. However, prolonged CRRT demonstrated the association of many unexpected events, such as catheter-related complications, catheter-related blood stream infection, hypotension, hypothermia, tachycardia, and atrial fibrillation. item.title: Lung Ultrasound-Guided Fluid Deresuscitation in ICU Patients
item.description: Timely recognition and treatment of fluid overload can expedite liberation from invasive mechanical ventilation in intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Lung ultrasound (LUS) is an easy to learn, safe, cheap and noninvasive bedside imaging tool with high accuracy for pulmonary edema and pleural effusions in ICU patients. item.title: Middle East Study of Infections in Patients With Hematological Malignancies
item.description: The goal of this prospective observational study is to is to prospectively study the epidemiology of bloodstream infection (BSI) in patients with hematological malignancies (HM) and hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) recipients across the Middle East. The objectives are to describe the epidemiological trends, identify risk factors for inappropriate antimicrobial therapy, and predictors of persistent BSI, microbiological relapse, and all-cause mortality. The study is entirely observational

item.title: EMCrit 437 – Massive Lithium Overdose
item.description: Massive lithium overdose is a once-or-twice-a-career case you cannot fumble. Toxicologist-nephrologist Josh King (Maryland Poison Center) walks through the crucial information and controversies EMCrit Project by Scott Weingart, MD FCCM .

item.title: Adrenal Function in Critical Illness
item.description: This study looked at how often adrenal insufficiency happens in critically ill patients and why it's a problem. They found that it occurs in up to 77% of cases, but there's no standard way to diagnose it. Researchers need to figure out how to identify and treat adrenal insufficiency.

item.title: NADPH Oxidase Correction in mRNA-transfected Granulocyte-enriched Cells in Chronic Granulomatous Disease (CGD)
item.description: Background: CGD is caused by a gene mutation. For people with CGD, their cells cannot kill germs well, so they can get frequent or life-threatening infections. Researchers want to see if a new procedure can help a person s cells kill germs for a short time. It uses messenger RNA (mRNA) to deliver correct instructions for the gene mutation to the cells. item.title: Chest U/S in Differentiating Lung Congestion & Pneumonia in Adult Critically-ill Patients and Its Prognostic Impact
item.description: This study aim will be to assess the effectiveness of chest ultrasound as a diagnostic and differentiating modality in cases of pneumonia and lung congestion . It also evaluates chests sonography effectiveness in follow-up of patients with pneumonia and lung congestion .

item.description: Mechanical ventilation is a critical intervention in the management of pediatric patients with respiratory distress. During this process, accurate measurement of transpulmonary pressure (PL) is essential to ensure the safety and efficacy of ventilation. PL is defined as the difference between alveolar pressure (Palv) and pleural pressure (Ppl). While the direct measurement of Ppl is possible, it poses a risk to tissue integrity. item.title: Abdominal Massage and Range-of-motion Exercise in Enterally Fed ICU Patients With Pressure Injuries
item.description: The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether two nursing interventions, lower abdominal massage and range-of-motion (ROM) exercises (gentle movements of the arm and leg joints), affect the healing of pressure injuries (bed sores) in intensive care patients who are fed through a tube (enteral nutrition). item.title: Patient- and Family-centred Care in the Adult Intensive Care Unit: a Feasibility Study
item.description: Background: In the intensive care unit (ICU), delirium in patients and long-term mental health challenges in both patients and their family members are highly prevalent. To address these issues, patient- and family-centered care has been recommended to alleviate the burdens associated with critical illness and ICU admission. item.description: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the impact of an avatar-supported, teacher-student interactive, vodcast-based peer bullying prevention program-developed for adolescents-on students' ability to identify peer bullying, their experiences with bullying, fighting, and victimization, and their levels of empathy. item.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
item.description: BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. item.title: Chlorhexidine within a standardized oral-care bundle for the prevention of ventilator-associated pneumonia: a pragmatic cluster-randomized crossover trial in six medical intensive care units.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Chlorhexidine (CHX) has been a long-standing component of oral-care bundles for preventing ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP), but recent evidence has questioned its benefit in non-cardiac-surgery ICU. We evaluated whether adding 0.12% CHX to standardized oral-care bundle provides incremental benefit in a mixed medical ICU. item.title: A Study to Evaluate AZD7760 Safety and Pharmacokinetics in Healthy Adults (Phase I) and Adults With End-stage Kidney Disease on Hemodialysis With a Central Venous Catheter (Phase IIa)
item.description: This study evaluated the safety and pharmacokinetics of AZD7760 in healthy adults and those with end-stage kidney disease on hemodialysis. Participants received AZD7760 as an intravenous infusion. The study aimed to assess the drug's safety and how it is absorbed and processed in the body.

item.title: CLARITHROMYCIN TO PREVENT SECONDARY INFECTIONS IN PATIENTS WITH SEPSIS FOLLOWING LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS: THE CLASSIFY TRIAL
item.description: The goal of this clinical trial is to assess whether clarithromycin, given as an adjunct to standard-of-care antibiotic therapy, can reduce the risk of new infections and secondary sepsis in adult patients hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), sepsis, and sepsis-induced immunoparalysis (SII). item.title: Detection and Characterization of Lower Respiratory Infections in Critically Ill Patients
item.description: This study is a prospective observation study for lower respiratory tract infections in medical intensive care unit. Microbiologic and clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with severe pneumonia in medical intensive care unit will be monitored and analyzed.

item.title: LoW Dose-Intensity vs. Standard Dose-Intensity COntinuous Renal ReplaceMent Therapy in Critically Ill Patients (WISDOM)
item.description: An estimated 10-15% of critically ill patients with acute kidney failure in the intensive care unit receive acute dialysis therapy. The majority of these patients initially receive a continuous form of dialysis therapy call continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Prior studies have suggested that higher CRRT dose-intensity improved health outcomes for these patients; however, this was not found in high-quality clinical trials. item.title: The Effect of Pink Noise and the Quiet Night Intervention on Sleep Parameters in Intensive Care Unit Patients: A Single-Center Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: Sleep disruption is common in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients and is often worsened by environmental noise and nighttime care activities. Poor sleep may negatively affect recovery and well-being. This single-center, three-arm randomized controlled trial will evaluate the short-term effects of two non-pharmacological interventions-(1) pink-brown noise masking and (2) a quiet time intervention-on objective sleep parameters in adult ICU patients, compared with standard care. item.title: Adverse Events During Physical Therapy in Neurocritical ICU Patients
item.description: The goal of this observational study is to identify the clinical, neurological, hemodynamic, and respiratory variables associated with the occurrence of adverse events during physical therapy interventions in adult neurocritical patients admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The main questions it aims to answer are: What clinical, neurological, hemodynamic, and respiratory factors are associated with adverse events during physical therapy in neurocritical patients? item.title: Clinical Value of EMR3 in Sepsis Diagnosis, Monitoring, and Prognosis: A Multicenter Prospective Observational Study
item.description: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition caused by a dysregulated immune response to infection, leading to organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Early diagnosis and accurate assessment of disease progression remain challenging. EMR3 (ADGRE3), a receptor expressed on the surface of neutrophils, may serve as a potential biomarker for sepsis diagnosis, immune response monitoring, and prognosis assessment. item.title: Automatic Tube Compensation vs. Pressure Support Ventilation During Spontaneous Breathing Trials in Adults
item.description: For patients requiring mechanical ventilation, spontaneous breathing trials (SBTs) are conducted to determine if it is safe to remove the breathing tube. There are multiple methods for conducting SBTs. The purpose of this study is to compare the effects of 2 methods, pressure support ventilation (PSV) versus automatic tube compensation (ATC), on successful extubation for critically ill adult patients who received mechanical ventilation for over 24 hours.

item.description: Millions of people are hospitalized every year in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) with severe health conditions due to various causes and categories of diseases, such as stroke, Traumatic Brain Injuries (TBI), polytrauma, sepsis, and others. In recent years, there has been a remarkable increase in survival rates among patients from all diagnostic categories admitted to the ICU. item.description: Sepsis is a dysregulated host response to infection that leads to life-threatening organ dysfunction and represents a major healthcare problem. Septic shock is the most severe form, characterized by increased capillary permeability and vasodilation, resulting in hypotension and tissue hypoxia. Early identification and treatment of tissue hypoperfusion are pivotal components of initial resuscitation to limit progression to multiple organ dysfunction and death. item.title: Metabolic and Functional Study of γδ T Cells in Critically Ill Patients
item.description: This prospective observational cohort study investigates the subset-specific metabolic adaptation and functional remodeling of cytotoxic γδ T cells in critically ill patients with and without sepsis. As a bridge between innate and adaptive immunity, γδ T cells contribute to early antimicrobial defense; however, their cytotoxic function and its metabolic regulation in sepsis remain incompletely understood. item.title: Respiratory Physiotherapy and PMR After Cardiac Surgery
item.description: This study aims to evaluate the effects of respiratory physiotherapy combined with progressive muscle relaxation exercises on dyspnea, anxiety, hemodynamic status, and delirium symptoms in patients after cardiac surgery. This randomized controlled trial will include 116 patients who will be randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. item.description: Shock is a common and serious cause of admission to intensive care. Vascular filling is one of the cornerstones of shock treatment, aimed at increasing cardiac output and restoring adequate organ perfusion through rapid intravenous administration of a solution. item.title: Cardiogenic Shock Working Group Registry
item.description: The Cardiogenic Shock Working Group is a multicenter registry where we collect de-identified clinical variables from the medical records and follow-up phone calls of shock patients from multiple institutions and centralize this data to a single registry for analysis of clinical outcomes.

item.title: Prevention of Arteriovenous Thrombotic Events in Critically-Ill COVID-19 Patients Trial
item.description: The researchers wanted to learn how to help sick patients who are in the hospital because of COVID-19. They are trying to find out the best way that is safe to stop blood clots that could be dangerous from forming in patients with COVID-19. This research study happened at 34 hospitals. All patients in the study took medicines that help prevent blood clots. These medicines are called blood thinners or anticoagulants. item.title: Humidification Effects on Airway Complications and Clinical Outcomes in Trauma ICU Patients on Mechanical Ventilation
item.description: This study compares the effects of two primary airway humidification methods-active heated humidifiers (HHs) and passive heat-and-moisture exchangers (HMEs)-on trauma intensive care unit (ICU) patients requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation. Adequate humidification is essential during mechanical ventilation because artificial airways bypass the body's natural ability to warm and moisten inhaled air. item.description: The pulmonary artery catheter (Swan-Ganz) is a standard tool in intensive care for measuring and monitoring cardiac index by thermodilution. The Swan-Ganz IQ™ model also allows continuous estimation of cardiac index through analysis of the right ventricular pressure wave, which could be useful for rapidly assessing changes in cardiac output during volume expansion response tests. item.title: Effect of Lactiplantibacillus Plantarum DAD-13 on Inflammatory Markers in ICU Sepsis Patients
item.description: This study investigated whether giving the probiotic Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DAD-13 to sepsis patients in the intensive care unit (ICU) could help reduce inflammation and improve bowel function. A total of 30 adult ICU patients with sepsis were randomly assigned to receive either the probiotic or a placebo for four days, along with standard treatment. item.description: This study aims to investigate whether combining cycling exercise with an immersive and interactive virtual reality (VR) environment improves motivation compared with cycling without visual support or cycling while watching a route on a television screen in critically ill patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). item.title: A Phase III, Open Label, Randomized, Controlled Study of VBI-S in the Treatment of Hypovolemia in Patients With Septic Shock (VBI-S-02)
item.description: This study is being conducted to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of VBI-S in elevating the blood pressure of septic shock patients with absolute or relative hypovolemia.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Readmission Reduction Interventions for Individuals With Sepsis or Pneumonia
item.description: An adaptive platform trial to compare effectiveness of different care models to prevent readmissions for patients hospitalized with sepsis or lower respiratory tract infection. The primary outcome is number of days spent at home within 90 days after hospital discharge.

item.description: Septic shock is a syndrome associated with severe infection and a mortality rate of approximately 45%. In line with current recommendations, norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor used in patients with septic shock. In a previous study, norepinephrine doses above 1 µg/kg/min were associated with mortality rates over 90%. In the same study, doses above 0.3 µg/kg/min were associated with a mortality rate of 40%. item.description: Approximately 40% of patients develop muscle dysfunction during their stay in intensive care, particularly in the context of sepsis. This dysfunction represents an acquired muscle injury that is secondary to the primary illness that led to ICU admission. item.description: Bacteremia, a common infection associated with high morbidity and mortality, requires prompt and appropriate antibiotic treatment. The aim of this study was to investigate the skeletal muscle anabolic response to combined resistance exercise and protein intake in intensive care unit (ICU) survivors, compared to matched controls without a history of critical illness. item.description: This study investigates the relationship between physiological dead space and clinical outcomes, specifically mortality and discharge status, in adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU). item.description: The purpose of this study is to collect a large amount of data that may assist in addressing the gap in knowledge of understanding pupillometer readings using a pupillometer device. The aim of this project is to establish normative values for pupillometer data. item.title: Real-time NOMA Evaluation
item.description: Alerts related to outlier clinician behavior are generated in real-time by an intelligent system continuously scraping EHR (electronic health record) data. These alerts are passed to the bedside and their potential impact on bedside clinical behavior is evaluated.

item.title: Clinical Trial of CG-BM1 Allogeneic Human Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cell Injection in the Treatment of Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
item.description: 1. To evaluate the safety and tolerability of CG-BM1 for the treatment of patients with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome. 2. To observe the preliminary effectiveness of CG-BM1 in treating Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome patients.

item.title: Pulmonary-Specific Enteral Nutrition in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Pneumonia
item.description: Pneumonia is a major cause of critical illness and respiratory failure, particularly among patients requiring invasive mechanical ventilation. These patients frequently experience systemic inflammation and metabolic disturbances, which can be assessed using the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and blood lactate levels. item.title: Comparison of Corticosteroids vs Placebo on Duration of Ventilatory Support During Severe Acute Exacerbations of COPD Patients in the ICU
item.description: The main objective of this study is to determine if the systemic (intravenous) administration of corticosteroids, as compared to placebo, increases the number of ventilator-free days (VFD) and alive at day 28 in COPD patients admitted to an ICU, a step-up unit or a respiratory care unit for an acute on chronic respiratory failure (ACRF) requiring ventilatory support, either invasive or non-invasive.

item.title: Protocol for Rapid Onset of Mobilization in Patients With Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury II (PROMPT-SCI II) Trial
item.description: Spinal cord injuries (SCI) are among the most catastrophic survivable events experienced by human beings. Affected individuals remain with lifelong neurological impairment involving motor, sensory, bladder and bowel functions, which in turn impacts quality of life and independence. item.description: Pneumonia is a lung infection that can cause serious complications, especially when accompanied by sepsis. Sepsis can trigger excessive inflammation and abnormal blood clotting, potentially leading to organ damage and delayed recovery. Two blood markers, D-dimer and interleukin-6 (IL-6), may increase in patients with these conditions. item.description: Many patients in intensive care (ICU) need help to breathe on a breathing machine and need pain killers and sedatives to keep them comfortable and pain free. However, keeping patients too deeply sedated can make their ICU stay longer, can cause ICU confusion (delirium) and afterwards may cause distressing memories. item.description: This is a pilot feasibility study examining the use of immersive virtual reality (VR) in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients.
